# @ratmath/symbolic

> Symbolic algebra for RatMath: expressions, rewriting, solving and closed forms, with every step checked by the certified libraries. Part of the RatMath Shelf; numbers come from @ratmath/core (a peer dependency). ESM: `import * as symbolic from "@ratmath/symbolic"`.

Built from 0.2.0, commit 82e737b. `file:line` is relative to the package root (also node_modules/@ratmath/symbolic/); on GitHub: https://github.com/ratmath/symbolic/blob/82e737b/<file>#L<line>. Docs pages are under https://ratmath.com/symbolic/. Full types: index.d.ts.

Types: `type ExprLike = string | Expr | Tree | number | bigint | Rational`; `type AssumptionOne = string | [number | string | Rational, number | string | Rational] | RationalInterval | Region`; `type AssumptionSpec = Record<string, AssumptionOne | AssumptionOne[]>`; `type Sign = "positive" | "negative" | "zero" | "nonnegative" | "nonpositive" | "nonzero" | "unknown"`; `type RuleSet = Rule | RuleSet[] | readonly RuleSet[] | { readonly [name: string]: RuleSet }`

## Docs

- https://ratmath.com/symbolic/llms-full.txt: every page below as Markdown, each with a runnable example
- Pages: index (Overview), reference (Reference), explore (Explore), expressions (Expressions), assumptions (Assumptions), normal-forms (Normal forms), rules (Rules), equality (Equality), solving (Solving equations), trig-equations (Trigonometric equations), systems (Systems of equations), inequalities (Inequalities), antiderivatives (Antiderivatives), limits (Limits), expansions (Expansions), sums (Sums), steps (Step records)

- `isZero(x: ExprLike, options?: NormalOptions) → boolean | "nonzero"` — True when the normal form is 0, "nonzero" when it is a nonzero number, else false (nothing proven). · src/normal.js:727 · reference

## Example

```js
import { sym, equal, solve, integrate, limit, solveSystem, sum, explain } from "@ratmath/symbolic";
// A classic: is this really 1?
const lhs = sym("(sqrt(5) + 1)/2 * (sqrt(5) - 1)/2");
console.log(lhs.toString(), "=", lhs.expand().toString());

// Three answers to "are these equal?"
for (const [a, b] of [
  ["cos(x)^4 - sin(x)^4", "cos(2x)"],
  ["sqrt(x^2 + 2x + 1)", "x + 1"],
  ["sqrt(x^2 + 2x + 1)", "abs(x + 1)"],
  ["exp(x)*exp(-x)", "1"],
  ["atan(1)", "pi/4"],
]) console.log(a, " vs ", b, " → ", equal(a, b).toString());

// With an assumption the second one becomes a proof
console.log(equal("sqrt(x^2 + 2x + 1)", "x + 1", { assume: { x: "> -1" } }).toString());

// Solving checks its candidates; integrating checks its answer
console.log(solve("sqrt(x + 3) = x - 3").toString());
console.log(integrate("x^2*sin(x)").toString());
console.log(limit("(1 - cos(x))/x^2", "x", 0).toString());

// Systems and sums, and the steps behind an answer
console.log(solveSystem(["x^2 + y^2 = 25", "x + y = 7"]).toString());
console.log(sum("k*2^k", "k", 0, "n").toString());
String(explain.solve("2sin(x)^2 = 1"))
```
